definitions.explanation: A strong, lasting feeling of hatred or bitterness toward someone, often stemming from a perceived wrong. Frequently appears in news reporting about criminal motives.

examples.japanese: {怨恨|えんこん}による{犯行|はんこう}。
examples.english: A crime motivated by a grudge.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{怨恨|えんこん}が{動機|どうき}とみている。
examples.english: The police believe resentment was the motive.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}にわたる{怨恨|えんこん}が、ついにこの{事件|じけん}を{引|ひ}き{起|お}こした。
examples.english: Years of accumulated resentment finally led to this incident.

notes:
Compound noun: {怨|えん} (resentment) + {恨|こん} (grudge). A formal, literary word most often encountered in news reports discussing criminal motives.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {怨恨|えんこん}による{犯行|はんこう} (a grudge-motivated crime)
- {怨恨|えんこん}が{動機|どうき} (resentment as the motive)
- {怨恨|えんこん}を{抱|いだ}く (to harbor a grudge)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {恨|うら}み: grudge, resentment — more common in everyday speech
- {怨恨|えんこん}: deeper, more formal term — often used in news and legal contexts
